Introduction

OVERVIEW: A learner's licence in India is a temporary driving permit that allows individuals to practice driving under supervision before obtaining a permanent driving licence. It is mandatory to obtain a learner's licence for the relevant vehicle class before applying for a permanent driving licence. This guide covers everything you need to know about learner's licences in India, including types, eligibility, required documents, application process (online and offline), test procedure, validity, and important rules. WHO IS THIS FOR: - First-time driving licence applicants - Individuals who have reached the minimum legal age for the respective vehicle class - Students, adults, and those who need to learn driving legally - People who want to practice driving on Indian roads under supervision - Applicants for both personal and commercial vehicle classes IMPORTANT NOTE: A learner's licence is valid for six months and allows you to practice driving only under the supervision of a person holding a valid permanent driving licence for the same vehicle class. You must display an 'L' sign on your vehicle and follow all traffic rules. After holding a learner's licence for at least 30 days, you can apply for a permanent driving licence. TABLE OF CONTENTS: 1. 1. WHAT IS A LEARNER'S LICENCE?

A learner's licence in India is a temporary driving permit issued to individuals who are at the learning stage of driving. It allows the holder to practice driving on public roads under the supervision of a person holding a valid permanent driving licence. The learner's licence is issued after the applicant passes a written or online test that assesses knowledge of traffic rules, road safety signals, and regulations.

Key points:
- Temporary permit for learning to drive
- Issued after passing a theory test
- Valid for six months
- Mandatory before obtaining a permanent driving licence
- Allows supervised driving practice on public roads

chunks.section: 2. TYPES OF LEARNER'S LICENCE IN INDIA
chunks.text:
2. TYPES OF LEARNER'S LICENCE IN INDIA

Learner's licences in India are issued based on the class of motor vehicle. Depending on the vehicle class, the eligibility criteria and application process may vary. The most common vehicle classes are:

PERSONAL USE VEHICLES:

MC 50CC (Motorcycle 50 cc)
- Motorcycles with engine capacity of 50 cc or less

LMV-NT
- Light Motor Vehicle used for non-transport (personal) purposes, such as cars

FVG
- Motorcycles of any engine capacity but without gears, such as scooters and mopeds

MC EX50CC
- Motorcycles with engine capacity of 50 cc or more, motorcycles with gear, and Light Motor Vehicles (LMVs) including cars

MCWG or M/CYCL.WG
- All types of motorcycles including motorcycles with gear

COMMERCIAL USE VEHICLES:

HGMV
- Heavy Goods Motor Vehicle

LMV-TR
- Light Motor Vehicle used for commercial (transport) purposes

HPMV
- Heavy Passenger Motor Vehicle / All India driving permit for trucks and cars

MGV
- Medium Goods Vehicle

3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

The eligibility criteria for a learner's licence depend on the vehicle class and type of licence sought.

Motorcycles with Gear:
- Minimum age: 18 years

Motorcycles without Gear (up to 50 cc capacity):
- Minimum age: 16 years
- Parental or guardian consent required if applicant is below 18 years

General Requirement:
- Minimum age: 18 years for most vehicle classes
- Must understand traffic rules and regulations
- Must have valid address proof and age proof documents

Commercial Heavy Vehicles and Transport Vehicles:
- Minimum age: 18 years (in some states, 20 years)
- Must have completed 8th standard of schooling

4. DETAILS PRESENT IN LEARNER'S LICENCE

The learner's licence contains the following important details:

- Name and age of the learner's licence holder
- Photograph of the applicant
- Issuing authority of the learner's licence
- A label specifying that it is a learner's licence
- Vehicle class for which the licence is issued
- Validity period (six months from date of issue)

5. APPLICATION FEES

Application Fee for Learner's Licence:
- Application fee: Rs. 150
- Test fee: Rs. 50
- Total: Rs. 200

Payment must be made at the time of submitting the application and required documents.

6. LEARNER'S LICENCE APPLICATION FORM

The application form for a learner's licence consists of two main sections:

Section 1: Particulars to be furnished by the applicant
The applicant must enter the following details:
- Personal details: name, address, date of birth, place of birth
- Educational qualification
- Type of Indian citizenship (by birth, naturalization) with supporting documentation
- Blood group
- Previous driving licences held, if any
- Driving school certificate, if applicable
- Exemption from medical test, if applicable

Section 2: Declaration
- Declaration that all entered particulars are true
- Signature of the parent/guardian of the applicant if applicant is below 18 years

The form can be downloaded from the state RTO website or obtained directly from the RTO office.

Microinstructions:
- Download form from RTO website or collect from RTO office.
- Fill Section 1 with accurate personal details.
- Fill Section 2 with declaration and signature.
- Attach photographs if required.

7. DOCUMENTS REQUIRED

To apply for a learner's licence, the following documents are required:

Proof of Address (any one):
- Recent electricity or telephone bill
- LIC Bond
- Aadhaar Card
- Passport
- House agreement
- Ration Card

Age Proof (any one):
- PAN Card
- Birth Certificate
- Transfer certificate from school with date of birth
- 10th class mark sheet
- Passport

Additional Requirements:
- At least six passport-size photographs
- Completely filled application form (Form 2 or Form 3)
- Medical Certificate (Form 1A and Form 1) signed by a certified government doctor, if applicable
- If residing in a city different from your permanent address, submit rental agreement with a recent utility bill

Microinstructions:
- Collect one valid proof of address.
- Collect one valid age proof.
- Get at least six passport-size photos.
- Download and fill the application form completely.
- Get medical certificate if applicable.
- Keep originals and copies ready.

8. HOW TO APPLY ONLINE

Many state RTO websites and the Parivahan portal offer online application for learner's licence. The general procedure is as follows: Step 1: Visit Your State RTO Website or Parivahan Portal - Open your state transport department or RTO website - Check if online learner's licence application is available Step 2: Fill Application Details - Enter required details: name, father's name, district, postal code, Aadhaar number, region - Select vehicle class - Upload required documents: proof of age, proof of address, photograph - Upload medical certificate if applicable Step 3: Pay Application Fee - Some RTOs allow online fee payment - Select test date and time slot if available - Pay Rs. 200 (Rs. 150 application fee + Rs. 50 test fee) through the online payment gateway - Download and save the payment receipt Step 4: Confirm Appointment - Download the application form or confirmation slip - Print the confirmation slip to present at the RTO or test centre - Save application reference number Step 5: Attend Test - Visit the RTO or test facility at the selected date and time - Carry original documents - Take the learner's licence test Microinstructions: - Open state RTO website or Parivahan portal. -

9. HOW TO APPLY OFFLINE

If you are not comfortable with online application or if your state RTO does not offer online application, you can apply directly at the RTO office.

Step 1: Obtain Application Form
- Obtain Form 2 or Form 3 from the RTO office
- Or download the form from the RTO website and print it

Step 2: Fill Application Form
- Fill the form completely and accurately
- Attach passport-size photographs if required
- Attach proof of address and age proof documents

Step 3: Submit at RTO
- Visit the nearest RTO office
- Submit the completed application form at the designated counter
- Pay the application fee (Rs. 200)
- Collect payment receipt

Step 4: Book Test Slot
- Schedule a learner's licence test appointment
- Note down the test date and time

Step 5: Attend Test
- Be present at the test facility on the scheduled date and time
- Pass the test to receive your learner's licence

Microinstructions:
- Collect Form 2 or Form 3.
- Fill completely.
- Attach photos and documents.
- Visit RTO.
- Submit form.
- Pay fee.
- Book test slot.
- Attend test.

10. TEST PROCEDURE

All learner's licence applicants must pass a written or online test that assesses their knowledge of traffic rules, road safety signals, and regulations. Test Procedure: Step 1: Reach Test Venue - Arrive at the test venue at least 30 minutes before the scheduled time Step 2: Understand Test Format - The test is usually a multiple-choice question (MCQ) test - Questions are based on traffic rules, road signs, and safety regulations - The test can be conducted on paper or online Step 3: Submit Documents - If you applied online, submit the confirmation slip at the counter - Pay any pending fees if applicable Step 4: Take the Test - Answer all multiple-choice questions - You must correctly answer a predetermined number of questions to pass Step 5: Result - Results are usually announced immediately or shortly after the test - If you pass, you will receive your learner's licence on the spot or it will be sent to your registered address - If you fail, you can retake the test after one week by paying the retest fee Important Points: - Study traffic rules and road signs before the test - Most RTOs provide study material or sample questions

chunks.section: 11. WHY YOU NEED A LEARNER'S LICENCE
chunks.text:
11. WHY YOU NEED A LEARNER'S LICENCE

Here are the key reasons why you need a learner's licence in India:
1. Legal Requirement:
   - To learn to drive a motor vehicle, you must first obtain a learner's licence for that vehicle class
   - A learner's licence legally allows you to practice driving on Indian roads
2. Supervised Practice:
   - You can practice driving with a person holding a valid permanent driving licence
   - This helps you develop and polish your driving skills before driving independently
3. Prerequisite for Permanent Driving Licence:
   - A learner's licence is a mandatory step before obtaining a permanent driving licence
   - It is easier to apply for a permanent driving licence if you hold a valid learner's licence
4. Road Familiarity:
   - Holding a learner's licence and practicing on roads helps you become familiar with road rules and real driving conditions
5. Insurance Requirement:
   - Most vehicle insurance policies in India require the driver to possess a valid driving licence, which includes a learner's licence during the learning phase

12. VALIDITY AND RENEWAL

Validity:
- A learner's licence is valid for six months from the date of issue
- It is valid throughout India

Renewal:
- An expired learner's licence cannot be renewed
- If your learner's licence expires, you must apply for a fresh learner's licence

Important Note:
- Apply for a permanent driving licence within six months of receiving your learner's licence
- You can apply for a permanent driving licence 30 days after receiving your learner's licence

Microinstructions:
- Note the issue date on your learner's licence.
- Calculate the expiry date (six months from issue).
- Apply for permanent driving licence before expiry.
- If expired, apply for fresh learner's licence.

13. IMPORTANT RULES AND RESTRICTIONS

While using a learner's licence, you must follow these rules:
1. Always be accompanied:
   - You must always be accompanied by a person holding a valid permanent driving licence for the same vehicle class
2. Display 'L' sign:
   - You must display an 'L' sign (Learner sign) on your vehicle at all times while practicing
3. Speed restrictions:
   - Learners are not allowed to drive above a certain speed limit (varies by state and vehicle class)
4. Follow all traffic rules:
   - You must obey all traffic signals, signs, and regulations
5. No solo driving:
   - You cannot drive alone without supervision
6. No commercial use:
   - A learner's licence does not allow you to drive for commercial purposes

Microinstructions:
- Always have a licensed driver with you.
- Display 'L' sign on vehicle.
- Follow speed limits.
- Obey all traffic rules.
- Do not drive alone.

14. COMMON ERRORS AND SOLUTIONS

Problem: Application rejected due to incomplete documents
Solution:
- Ensure all required documents are submitted
- Check document validity (e.g., recent utility bills)
- Submit clear copies of documents

Problem: Failed the learner's licence test
Solution:
- Study traffic rules and road signs thoroughly
- Use sample test questions available online or at RTO
- Retake the test after one week by paying retest fee

Problem: Learner's licence expired
Solution:
- An expired learner's licence cannot be renewed
- Apply for a fresh learner's licence

Problem: Lost learner's licence
Solution:
- Contact your RTO for duplicate learner's licence issuance
- Pay applicable duplicate licence fee

Problem: Forgot to book test slot
Solution:
- Rebook test slot through RTO website or visit RTO office
- Pay applicable fees if required

Problem: Could not attend scheduled test
Solution:
- Rebook test slot
- Pay retest fee if applicable

15. FAQS

Question: Is my learner's licence valid throughout India? Answer: Yes, your learner's licence is valid throughout India for six months from the date of issue. Question: Are there any rules that must be followed while learning to drive with a learner's licence? Answer: Yes. You must be accompanied by a licensed driver, display an 'L' sign, follow speed restrictions, and obey all traffic rules. Question: What is the validity period of a learner's licence issued in India? Answer: A learner's licence is valid for six months. Question: Will I be asked to drive a motor vehicle to get my learner's licence? Answer: No. The learner's licence test is a written or online theory test only. Question: I need to apply for a learner's licence for a non-gear vehicle and a car. Do I have to apply separately? Answer: You can apply for both in one application and take a combined test, but separate fees apply. Question: Can I renew my learner's licence after it expires? Answer: No. An expired learner's licence cannot be renewed. You must apply for a fresh learner's licence. Question: Can an illiterate individual apply for a learner's licence? Answer: You will have to book a fresh appointment and pay the retest fee. Question: How can I check the status of my learner's licence application? Answer: You can check the status on the official Parivahan Sewa website or your state RTO website. Question: Is my learner's licence valid for commercial vehicles? It is compulsory to display an 'L' sign to indicate you are learning. Question: Is a learning licence issued for a bike? Answer: Yes. A learner's licence is issued for two-wheelers based on the vehicle class selected.

FINAL USER REMINDER

15. FAQS

Before submitting your learner's licence application, ensure all details are accurate, all required documents are attached, and payment is completed. Study traffic rules and road signs thoroughly before the test. Always follow learner's licence rules and restrictions while practicing. Apply for a permanent driving licence within six months of receiving your learner's licence. Keep your learner's licence, receipts, and documents safe.

15. FAQS

ADDITIONAL BEST-PRACTICE NOTES

15. FAQS

- Always carry original documents for verification
- Keep copies of all receipts and acknowledgements
- Study traffic rules regularly
- Practice driving only under proper supervision
- Display 'L' sign at all times while learning
- Follow all speed restrictions
- Apply for permanent driving licence before learner's licence expires
- Keep mobile number and address updated on the application

108. Submit the test.
109. Wait for the result.

SECTION J: AFTER THE TEST

110. If you pass, collect your learner's licence.
111. Some RTOs issue the licence on the spot.
112. Some RTOs send the licence to your registered address.
113. Check all details on the learner's licence immediately.
114. Verify name, date of birth, photograph, and vehicle class.
115. Keep the learner's licence safely.
116. If you fail, ask about the retest process.
117. Pay the retest fee if applicable.

SECTION K: USING LEARNER'S LICENCE

120. Always carry your learner's licence while practicing driving.
121. Always be accompanied by a person holding a valid permanent driving licence for the same vehicle class.
122. Display an 'L' sign on your vehicle.
123. Follow all traffic rules.
124. Do not exceed speed limits applicable to learners.
125. Do not drive alone.
126. Practice regularly under supervision.
127. Familiarize yourself with road rules.

chunks.text:
SECTION L: APPLYING FOR PERMANENT DRIVING LICENCE

129. Wait for at least 30 days after receiving your learner's licence.
130. Apply for a permanent driving licence after 30 days.
131. Book a driving test slot.
132. Practice driving skills thoroughly before the driving test.
133. Attend the driving test at the RTO.
134. Pass the driving test.
135. Collect your permanent driving licence.

SECTION M: VALIDITY AND RENEWAL

136. Remember that learner's licence is valid for six months only.
137. Apply for permanent driving licence before the learner's licence expires.
138. If learner's licence expires, you cannot renew it.
139. Apply for a fresh learner's licence if expired.
